 Brewers' Rule 5 Draft-eligible prospect could have important role in 2027 first base plans 
 Don't forget about top prospect Luke Adams as the Brewers sort out their 2027 roster. By Owen Jonas | Nov 10, 2026, 6:02 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Milwaukee Brewers infielder Luke Adams plays catch during spring training workouts Tuesday, February 17, 2026, at American Family Fields of Phoenix in Phoenix, Arizona. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Milwaukee Brewers are set to return a large portion of their 2026 World Series-winning roster for the 2027 campaign. From a starting rotation that was made up almost entirely of players in the first two seasons of their MLB careers to a young core of position players that includes Jackson Chourio, Cooper Pratt, Brice Turang, and Luis Lara, the Brewers' World Series title is by no means closing the franchise's window of contention.
--> The Milwaukee Brewers are set to return a large portion of their 2026 World Series-winning roster for the 2027 campaign. From a starting rotation that was made up almost entirely of players in the first two seasons of their MLB careers to a young core of position players that includes Jackson Chourio, Cooper Pratt, Brice Turang, and Luis Lara, the Brewers' World Series title is by no means closing the franchise's window of contention.
 However, as Brewers fans enjoy the fruits of their front office's forward-thinking roster construction strategy, there are still several personnel questions that Matt Arnold and his team must answer before the 2027 season arrives. Chief among said remaining questions is the Brewers' plan at first base.

Chief among said remaining questions is the Brewers' plan at first base.
 In 2026, the Brewers relied on one of the most productive platoons in baseball -- left-handed hitting Jake Bauers and right-handed hitting Andrew Vaughn -- at first base. Between Bauers' breakout season at the plate and Vaughn's dominance against southpaws, Milwaukee's duo of first basemen was key to the team's record-breaking season. However, it's unlikely the platoon remains intact in 2027.
--> In 2026, the Brewers relied on one of the most productive platoons in baseball -- left-handed hitting Jake Bauers and right-handed hitting Andrew Vaughn -- at first base. Between Bauers' breakout season at the plate and Vaughn's dominance against southpaws, Milwaukee's duo of first basemen was key to the team's record-breaking season. However, it's unlikely the platoon remains intact in 2027.
 Bauers is currently deciding whether or not to accept the Brewers' $23.15 million qualifying offer, which would keep him in Milwaukee for one additional season. It would represent a significant raise for Bauers, who made just $2.7 million in 2026, but it's also likely the breakout slugger could earn more guaranteed money on the free agent market. Vaughn, meanwhile, is projected by MLB Trade Rumors to earn $8.5 million in his final year of arbitration . Therefore, if Bauers were to accept the qualifying offer and Vaughn was to be retained at his projected salary, the Brewers would be paying their first baseman a collective $31.65 million in 2027 -- something the savvy Milwaukee front office appears unlikely to do.

Therefore, if Bauers were to accept the qualifying offer and Vaughn was to be retained at his projected salary, the Brewers would be paying their first baseman a collective $31.65 million in 2027 -- something the savvy Milwaukee front office appears unlikely to do.
 Therefore, if Bauers does accept the qualifying offer, expect the Brewers to field trade offers for Vaughn, who will hit free agency at the end of the 2027 season. In such a scenario, or if Vaughn ends up being Milwaukee's everyday first baseman in 2027, expect top prospect Luke Adams, who spent the 2026 season in Triple-A, to have a role on Milwaukee's big-league club next season.

In such a scenario, or if Vaughn ends up being Milwaukee's everyday first baseman in 2027, expect top prospect Luke Adams, who spent the 2026 season in Triple-A, to have a role on Milwaukee's big-league club next season.
 Corner infield prospect Luke Adams is all but certain to factor into Brewers' 2027 first base plans
--> Corner infield prospect Luke Adams is all but certain to factor into Brewers' 2027 first base plans
 The 22-year-old Adams, who the Brewers drafted in the 12th round of the 2022 draft, currently checks in as Milwaukee's No. 13-ranked prospect according to MLB Pipeline, but previously resided in the Top 10. His movement is by no means due to his own level of play, which has been steadily strong throughout his time in the organization, but is rather due to the crowded nature of the Brewers' talented farm system. Adams, who played 67 games for the Triple-A Nashville Sounds as he battled several injuries during the 2026 campaign, is now knocking on the door of the big leagues and could play an important role in 2027.

Adams, who played 67 games for the Triple-A Nashville Sounds as he battled several injuries during the 2026 campaign, is now knocking on the door of the big leagues and could play an important role in 2027.
 The right-handed hitting Adams would be the perfect complement to Bauers at first base, if the latter accepts the qualifying offer and the Brewers elect to trade Vaughn. Playing on the league minimum salary, Adams would be more than $7 million cheaper than Vaughn -- a discrepancy that likely wouldn't be reflected in the two's difference in production. After all, Adams holds a career on-base percentage of .423 and a slugging percentage of .441 through five seasons in the minor leagues .

 Even if it's the right-handed hitting Vaughn who remains with the Brewers through the offseason, Adams could be a strong back-up option at first base. Adams has hit both righties and lefties well during his minor league career, so worries of him being a strict platoon option at first base aren't too severe.

 Additionally, though Adams has played more first base as he's reached the upper levels of the minor leagues and profiles as a first baseman in the big leagues, he does have the ability to man third base defensively as well. The 6'4" Adams is impressively athletic for his size and can hold his own at the hot corner, but will likely see most of his major league opportunities as a first baseman.

 Adams is Rule 5 Draft eligible this winter, meaning the Brewers have to add him to their 40-man roster or risk another team stealing him for nothing. It must be noted that the Rule 5 Draft is likely to be cancelled as a result of MLB's upcoming work stoppage, but teams must still prepare as if it is going to happen, considering the league could reschedule it after the lockout ends. With plenty of spots open, expect the Brewers to add Adams to their 40-man roster before the end of the month.
